ai_show_review.summary: Groovy blues set with Hard To Handle, King Bee and seamless Other One
ai_show_review.blurb: The April‑18 1969 Purdue show rides a steady groove, highlighted by Pigpen’s rousing Hard To Handle, a scorching King Bee and an uninterrupted Other One sandwich. Lovelight soars in the second half while Morning Dew closes the set on a high note. Overall playing is strong despite occasional mix quirks.
ai_show_review.review: On April 18, 1969 the Grateful Dead took over Purdue’s Memorial Union Ballroom with a blues‑heavy first set that still feels fresh today. Pigpen leads the charge on “Hard To Handle” and “I’m A King Bee,” his organ buzz‑saw riffs cutting through a mix that, while generally crisp thanks to Charlie Miller’s transfer, occasionally buries Jerry’s guitar – though his slide work on the opener shines. Phil Lesh provides a deep, resonant foundation, especially during the soaring opening of The Other One after the drum solo, even if one listener noted a flatter tone on this night. The centerpiece is the Cryptical Envelopment → Drums → The Other One → Cryptical sandwich, a seamless 20‑minute journey that builds into a powerful “Morning Dew.” The set rounds out with an epic “Turn On Your Lovelight” and a playful “Cosmic Charlie,” leaving the audience buzzing despite a mid‑first‑song power outage that briefly halted the flow. Both available soundboard recordings capture the energy well, but Miller’s version offers the clearest overall picture of this groove‑laden performance.

best_recording.reason: Highest clarity soundboard mix with crisp balance; captures the full set without dropouts.

key_highlights: Pigpen‑driven blues showcase on Hard To Handle and King Bee
Seamless Cryptical Envelopment → Drums → The Other One sandwich
Lovelight soars in the second half, leading into a powerful Morning Dew
Good overall soundboard quality despite occasional buried guitar

band_performance.Jerry: Slide work on Hard To Handle shines, though his guitar can dip into the background in places.
band_performance.Phil: Bass is solid and especially luminous during The Other One opening; one note of flatness mentioned but overall strong.
band_performance.Brent: Pigpen delivers bluesy buzz‑saw organ riffs on Hard To Handle, King Bee and Lovelight with vocal enthusiasm throughout.
